Nia: quick sync after the weekendincident - sketched an alternative to hard preemption: burst-crediting + soft-debt admission. want quick runtime tradeoff feedback.
Omar: TL;DR?
Nia: each tenant has a credit balance (token-bucket-like). normal refill = baseline. bursts can go negative to a soft_limit. scheduler biases away from deep-debt tenants and applies graceful fastpath switches when they exceed thresholds.
Priya: so we avoid instant 429s but still protect others. how does batcher change?
Nia: two small changes: 1) debt-aware packing - avoid mixing heavy-debt requests with green ones unless slack exists; 2) shrink coalesce window for debt tenants and prefer single-request fastpath when debt>soft_limit.
Omar: single-request fastpath = more kv warmups, risk of cache churn. any mitigation?
Nia: micro-prefix cache for surge tenants only (tiny, e.g. 2MB cap) and eviction hints to preserve warming keys briefly.
Priya: memory pressure concerns if many tenants surge concurrently.
Nia: we enforce a cluster_surge_budget. if aggregate micro-cache exceeds that we fall back to hard rejects for lowest-priority debt tenants.
infra-bot: cluster_surge_budget=200MB used=12MB
Omar: scheduling complexity? comparator and packer need changes. perf hit risk?
Nia: comparator is O(1) per enqueue - tag with debt_bucket (green/yellow/red). packer inspects head-of-queue and stops mixing when mixing_limit hit (default 25% tokens from red).
Priya: observability?
Nia: add metrics: tenant.credit_balance, tenant.debt_age, packer.mix_ratio_by_bucket, micro_cache_mem_used. Alerts if many tenants > soft_limit >2m or micro_cache_mem>80% budget.
Jules: rollout plan?
Nia: phased: metrics-only -> comparator tagging (no behavior change) -> packer limits + micro-cache in staging -> prod canary with feature flag + metric gates.
Omar: client-visible behavior: prefer clear signals. return 429 for hard_limit, accept with header X-Redwood-Debt=soft for soft. SDK notes needed.
Priya: open items: exact numeric defaults (soft_limit/hard_limit/refill_rate), cluster_surge_budget default. Ops to propose.
Nia: I'll draft RFC w/ sequence diagrams and knobs: refill_rate, soft_limit, hard_limit, mixing_limit, micro_cache_per_tenant_cap. tagging @Omar @Priya @infra. thanks for the quick review.
